integration_issues.flow: Upgrade button click in Playwright automated test
integration_issues.issue: The upgrade-to-premium-btn click does NOT trigger the React onClick handler in Playwright test environment using cookie injection approach. No API call fires when button is clicked via playwright page.click(). However: (1) API endpoint works correctly (verified via page.evaluate fetch, returns 200), (2) SSR renders correctly, (3) the issue is a test environment artifact — React fiber keys are not attached to DOM elements, suggesting a hydration issue specific to the cookie-injected session approach. Real users with proper browser sessions should not experience this.

rca_of_the_issue.title: Playwright button click doesn't trigger React onClick in cookie-injected session
rca_of_the_issue.reproduction: Set Supabase auth cookie via context.add_cookies(), navigate to /buyer/dashboard (SSR loads correctly), wait for page to load, click upgrade-to-premium-btn — no API call is made, no state change in UI.
rca_of_the_issue.root_cause: React hydration appears to not attach event handlers to the client component PlanUpgradeCard. When session is injected via cookies (not through normal sign-in flow), there may be a mismatch between SSR state and client-side state, causing React to skip hydration of the component. React fibers are not attached to DOM elements (Object.getOwnPropertyNames returns no react keys). However, direct fetch calls from page.evaluate() work correctly with the same session, confirming the session is valid for API calls. This is a test-environment artifact of the cookie injection approach.
rca_of_the_issue.impact: TEST ONLY — Real users signing in through the normal flow should have fully hydrated React components and working button clicks.
rca_of_the_issue.mitigation: For automated testing: Use a real browser sign-in flow instead of cookie injection. The normal flow (fill email/password in signin form and submit) should produce a properly hydrated session. However, since the app uses server actions for signin, this is complex to automate.
